title: Separate fuel from oxidizer with one move
instruction: No blue fuel canister may stand in a bay that shares a wall with a bay holding an orange oxidizer canister. Fix the rack by moving as few canisters as possible, and leave every canister upright in a bay.
context: A 1 g bench mock-up of a compartment segregation rule for propellant sample canisters in a payload processing facility. Hypergolic fuel and oxidizer ignite on contact. Real sites keep the two in separate areas; the rack stands for that rule, with a shared wall as too little separation. Every move of a loaded container is a hazardous step. The rack starts out of compliance: one blue fuel canister shares a wall with both orange oxidizer canisters. The test is the least intervention that removes the hazard, counted in canisters moved out of their start bays. One move fixes it, that fuel canister into the one empty bay with no oxidizer neighbour. The nearer empty bay sits next to oxidizer, moving either oxidizer canister alone leaves a breach, and a rebuild takes more moves and scores less. A breach, a canister out of a bay or two in one bay scores 0. The colours are codes the instruction defines. No propellant or reaction is simulated, and no microgravity is claimed.
setup: Station table, in front of the left arm; the right arm is idle at its ready pose. Table coordinates in metres: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left from the midline; the left arm's base is at (0, 0.305) and the table top is z = 0.7475 m. Every part is a rigid matte primitive with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Fixed, dark grey (sRGB 0.12, 0.12, 0.12), dark against the light wood table: a storage rack of dividers 6 mm thick and 15 mm tall standing on the table, forming two rows of four square bays at 90 mm pitch, each 84 x 84 mm inside and open to the table, so the table is each bay's floor. The rack's outer size is 186 x 366 mm, spanning x 0.142 to 0.328 and y 0.062 to 0.428. Three long dividers 6 x 366 x 15 mm (x, y, z) run along y, centred at y = 0.245 and x = 0.145, 0.235 and 0.325. Ten short dividers 84 x 6 x 15 mm run along x between them, centred at x = 0.190 and 0.280, each at y = 0.425, 0.335, 0.245, 0.155 and 0.065. Bay centres: row A (near) at x = 0.190 and row B (far) at x = 0.280; columns 1 to 4 at y = 0.380, 0.290, 0.200 and 0.110, column 1 outboard. Loose: six canisters, upright cylinders 40 mm in diameter and 60 mm tall, 90 g each (printed PLA at near-full infill), each standing at the centre of its bay. Blue (sRGB 0.15, 0.35, 0.85) fuel in A1 and A2; orange (sRGB 0.95, 0.50, 0.10) oxidizer in A3 and B2; white (sRGB 0.92, 0.92, 0.92) inert in A4 and B1. B3 and B4 are empty. Neighbouring canisters stand 90 mm apart centre to centre, with 50 mm of air between them, and each has 22 mm of clearance to every wall of its bay. The farthest bay, B4, is 0.34 m from the left arm's base. To build it: glue 6 x 15 mm strips (wood, acrylic or printed), painted dark grey, at the stated centres straight onto the table or onto a sheet at most 1 mm thick taped to it. Print the canisters in PLA at near-full infill (solid PLA would weigh 94 g), trim each to 90 g, paint two blue, two orange and two white, and write each one's start bay (A1, A2, A3, B2, A4, B1) on its top in 8 mm black letters, so a photo shows which canister moved; the simulated canisters are plain.
scoring: End state only, judged after the arm has released and moved clear, from a top photo, a tape measure and a phone level. A canister is in a bay when it stands on either end with its axis within 10 degrees of vertical, its lowest point within 3 mm of the table and its centre inside that bay's 84 x 84 mm inner outline, at rest (under 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s). Standing on the table between the 15 mm walls, a canister whose centre is inside a bay is wholly inside it. Gate, score 0: any canister in no bay (lying, leaning past 10 degrees, on a divider, on another canister, outside the rack, off the table, held up or still moving), two canisters in one bay, or a blue canister in a bay that shares a wall with a bay holding an orange canister. Two bays share a wall when they sit side by side in a row or front to back in a column; diagonal bays meet only at a corner and do not. White canisters may stand in any bay. The start layout breaches twice (A2 with A3, A2 with B2) and scores 0. Otherwise count the canisters moved: those standing in a bay other than their own start bay (in simulation each canister is known by name, on the real rig by the start-bay label on its top). A canister nudged, or lifted and set back, inside its own bay is no move; two of one colour that trade bays are two moves. One moved scores 1.0, two 0.6, three or more 0.3. Of the 20,160 end layouts with one canister per bay, exactly one scores 1.0: the blue canister from A2 in B4, every other canister in its start bay. Bay B3 shares walls with both orange bays, and moving either orange canister alone, or any other single canister, leaves a breach. Nine layouts score 0.6 (for example both orange canisters into B3 and B4, the fix plus a white canister moved, or the A1 blue canister into B4 and the A2 one into the freed A1), and 2,390, every compliant layout with three or more moved, a full rebuild included, score 0.3. Success, which ends the trial, is 1.0 held for 1 s. In simulation every test uses each canister's centre and axis (its lowest point from its centre, length and tilt), not its axis-aligned bounds, and a lowest point exactly 3.0 mm up counts (0.1 mm epsilon). The rack is fixed in simulation; on the real rig, a trial in which a divider moves more than 5 mm from its mark scores 0, and heights are measured from the surface the rack stands on (the table or its floor sheet). The scorer reads object poses, not the grippers: in simulation a canister held motionless within 3 mm of the table would count; on real arms the photo after the arm parks decides.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand each canister back at the centre of its own start bay, by the label on its top: blue in A1 and A2, orange in A3 and B2, white in A4 and B1, with B3 and B4 empty. The rack does not move. Run with -E object_jitter=0: the open-loop demo depends on it.
fidelity: Approximate: the canisters are rigid 90 g cylinders with no valves, caps or handles, and the colours only stand for fuel, oxidizer and inert; no propellant, leak or reaction is simulated. A shared wall stands in for a separation distance. Moves are counted from the end state, so a canister set back in its own bay is not counted, and the carry path is not scored. Real canister tops carry a start-bay label the simulated ones lack. Rigid primitives, one shared friction, Earth gravity on a bench.
